title: Redwood May 2026 All-Hands
summary: Monthly company all-hands: Lena opened with a business update (usage, revenue, hiring cadence). Marco covered technical milestones (latency SLOs, Dedicated pool launch progress, private deployment beta). Samir walked through product roadmap and Optimize features. Jill addressed reliability incidents and upcoming infra changes. Q&A covered pricing, SOC 2 timeline, and hiring. Action items and next steps captured at the end.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hello everyone, thanks for joining, happy May all-hands. quick note we hit some important milestones this quarter — I'll go through numbers and then hand off.
[00:22] Marco Ruiz: hi all, will jump in on the infra side — we've rolled a new batching shim that's shaving off about 8 to 12 ms p50 on our hosted endpoints, caveat, numbers vary by model and sequence length.
[00:45] Speaker 1: (inaudible) 
[00:50] Lena Park: okay, quick company numbers, revenue up 28% q/q, usage up 44%, net-new enterprise customers kind of steady — Rohit will talk sales in a bit. churn is low but we saw a couple of small self-serve accounts leave due to price sensitivity.
[01:20] Rohit Menon: yeah, qualification is the same, a lot of buyers are comparing Dedicated vs hosted cost economics, and the big asks are: private VPC, SOC 2, and predictable latency. we closed two mid-market deals this month, one with a healthcare ISV — they needed on-prem options.
[01:50] Samir Patel: on product, Optimize has new suggestions pipeline — we now surface quantization profile recs and batch size tuning per-route, it's in alpha and a handful of customers are testing. feature list: profile suggestions, rerank tuning, and eval hooks.
[02:10] Marco Ruiz: for dedicated, the dedicated pool autoscaler has one remaining issue: under heavy burst traffic we occasionally miscalculate GPU assignments and end up with cold starts. Jill will cover the postmortem.
[02:35] Jill Thompson: quick reliability note — last week we had an incident around 03:00 UTC where a kube autoscaler mislabel pushed nodes into a pending state; root cause was a config drift combined with a rollout that touched our custom scheduler. we mitigated by rolling back and adding an automated canary for the scheduler.
[03:05] Speaker 2: sorry timing question on that, are we adding a manual kill switch?
[03:10] Jill Thompson: yes, we've added an ops kill switch and a UI toggle for the scheduler; also improving alerting so the on-call sees the exact failure path.
[03:30] Lena Park: hiring — we continue to hire across infra and product, target headcount this quarter is +12, priority roles are backend infra, site reliability, and a senior product manager for Optimize.
[03:50] Emily Davis: on marketing, we're shipping a partner benchmark whitepaper next week — please review the draft in the marketing drive, link in the doc thread.
[04:05] Marco Ruiz: security/compliance, SOC 2 Type I is nearly complete, working toward Type II timeline — we've handed over logs to the auditor, encryption at rest with KMS is implemented for hosted, private customers can bring their own KMS, there's one remaining action item on key rotation docs.
[04:35] Priya Sharma: customers asking about detailed audit logs and retention — we have a roadmap item to increase retention windows for Dedicated and Private.
[04:50] Samir Patel: product roadmap highlights: 1) Optimize GA in Q3, 2) expanded model catalog with 3rd-party curated variants, 3) function/tool calling improvements (we're standardizing the schema), and 4) embeddings auto-indexing.
[05:20] Marco Ruiz: on the runtime, we've been testing grouped KV cache evictions, it's reduced memory churn by ~15% on long convo sessions. small caveat: some older model variants still have suboptimal kernel paths so we plan targeted kernel tuning.
[05:50] Audience Q: (text) any update on price adjustments?
[05:55] Lena Park: no immediate price changes; we're evaluating packaging to make Dedicated more attractive; any sales asks go to Rohit and finance.
[06:10] Rohit Menon: on Dedicated pricing we are experimenting with burst credits and committed throughput discounts, will pilot with three customers.
[06:30] Kai Nguyen: quick DS note — new eval harness is catching some hallucination regressions on one open model; we'll make a PR to add a new metric and run nightly checks.
[06:50] Samir Patel: that ties into quality monitoring in Optimize — we'll surface regression alerts tied to prompt suites; if a model drifts we can auto-block or flag.
[07:10] Speaker 3: cross talk ok can someone share the roadmap doc?
[07:15] Samir Patel: yes, link in the slack channel #product-roadmap, and I'll send the deck after.
[07:28] Lena Park: quick note on ops maturity: we're pushing more of the canary rollout logic into the control plane so Private customers can get the same rollback guarantees.
[07:45] Jill Thompson: and for Private/on-prem we are packaging an air-gapped installer that doesn't require outbound access during install — currently beta with two customers.
[08:10] Emily Davis: marketing ask: we need one pager for Private deployment features to help SDRs qualify.
[08:20] Priya Sharma: CS will draft a one-pager and share by EOD Friday.
[08:35] Marco Ruiz: technical deep dive planned next week on kernel selection heuristics for folks interested in the runtime internals — will be recorded.
[08:50] Audience: (laughs) good, more nerdy content!
[09:00] Lena Park: Q&A time — please drop questions in the meeting thread, we'll try to get to as many as possible.
[09:15] Speaker 4: question about model pins — can customers pin to a specific model sha?
[09:22] Samir Patel: yes, customers can pin to model versions; we're working on a nicer UI to manage rollouts and canaries across versions.
[09:40] Speaker 5: any update on EU region expansion?
[09:45] Marco Ruiz: we launched a second EU region in Amsterdam, latency improved for EU customers, still working on data residency SOC paperwork for a couple of countries.
[10:00] Lena Park: finance update — burn is tracking to plan, we have runway into next year with some assumptions, looking to tighten hiring cadence if we see slower enterprise ramp.
[10:20] Jill Thompson: short note on observability — new trace sampling has reduced storage costs while keeping high-fidelity traces for alerts.
[10:35] Kai Nguyen: are we comfortable exposing trace hooks to customers?
[10:40] Marco Ruiz: yes, with RBAC and filtered PII scrubbing; we will provide a sanitized stream for customers with opt-in.
[11:00] Lena Park: okay, recap: Samir will send roadmap deck, Jill will publish the postmortem and the ops kill switch runbook, Priya will draft Private one-pager, Marco will schedule the kernel-deep-dive, Rohit will identify pilot customers for Dedicated pricing.
[11:30] Samir Patel: I'll add the Optimize GA checklist and a short timeline to the deck.
[11:40] Lena Park: last call — shoutouts: infra shipped a tough rollout, great work on SOC 2. big thanks.
[12:00] Audience: applause (emoji in chat).
[12:15] Lena Park: meeting ends, see the notes and action items in the shared drive.
[62:00] Meeting ended.
